New Games category: representative listing/index template and route navigation.
Friday Night Funkin game detail: representative primary play journey, metadata and embedded game surface.
Editorial blog archetype. Screenshot loaded; subsequent probe encountered Yandex SmartCaptcha, retained as evidence of the explicit challenge/recovery state.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the entire catalog on first load.
findings.evidence: The desktop and mobile screenshots show a modal consent panel and dimmed backdrop covering the primary game catalog before interaction; the DOM probe reports a visible 512×396 role=dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface for non-essential processing; defer advertising requests until choice and preserve an equally prominent reject/manage path.

findings.summary: The interface uses one fixed dark palette rather than responding to the system color scheme.
findings.evidence: Dark-condition screenshot is effectively unchanged, and inspected CSS contained no prefers-color-scheme rule or color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Animation continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion CDP probe confirmed the media query matched but still found a running 1000 ms animation; inspected CSS contained no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or greatly shorten non-essential animation inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Catalog route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS/DOM inspection found no view-transition declarations or document.startViewTransition use on the representative home/category route templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document view transitions for catalog navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Header menus and transient panels are manually positioned rather than anchor-positioned.
findings.evidence: The inspected stylesheet contains no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try use despite multiple header controls and overlays.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for header menus/tooltips.

findings.summary: Consent and preference overlays are custom role=dialog divs rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM probe reports visible DIV role=dialog overlays and no native dialog or popover surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with <dialog> and transient panels with popover, preserving focus and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: The mobile layout renders at twice the visual viewport width.
findings.evidence: At 360×800, layout metrics report scrollWidth/innerWidth 720, visualViewportWidth 360, and 360 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot shows a desktop-width consent surface squeezed into mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed/minimum widths, make the consent surface fit 100% of the visual viewport, and test intrinsic layout at 320–400 px.

findings.summary: Reusable catalog components rely on viewport styling rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: The captured active stylesheet contained no @container rules while cards and panels are reused across the sidebar, grid, and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable panels/card groups containment and adapt them with size container queries.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on primary controls.
findings.evidence: After programmatically focusing visible controls, computed outlines repeatedly remained style none/0 px; several icon controls are only 32–40 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and ensure interactive targets are at least 44 CSS px where practical.

findings.summary: The mobile page is slow to become useful and interactive.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP/FCP 3.6 s, Speed Index 8.5 s and Time to Interactive 14.0 s (performance 0.74); trace corroborated LCP 2.28 s and two long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the catalog LCP, delay ad/analytics initialization, and split/defer non-critical application work.

findings.summary: Initial delivery is heavy and dependency-rich.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 153 requests and 5,042,724 transferred bytes, including 1.71 MB script, 1.34 MB fetch/XHR and 498 KB fonts; Lighthouse estimated 361 KiB cache savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Set durable caching for versioned assets, reduce font variants, shorten redirects, and gate non-critical third-party dependencies.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 614 KiB unused JavaScript and 186 KiB unused CSS; several bundles were 50–99% unused in the tested viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split catalog features and load advertising, notifications and account widgets only on demand.

findings.summary: Icon buttons and role=button controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility found unnamed burger, search-focus and account role=button elements plus an unnamed notifications <button>.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native buttons and give every icon-only control an aria-label or visible accessible name.

findings.summary: Inline game links are distinguishable only by low-contrast color.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 1.84:1 contrast between #58d854 links and surrounding white text, below the 3:1 non-color cue threshold, with no underline.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase link contrast and add an underline or another non-color indicator.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and heading structure are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Focus probe found no visible outline on primary controls; the homepage starts with an H3 before H1 and the consent widget injects several additional H1s.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore visible focus, keep one page H1, and structure modal headings within the dialog rather than as page-level H1s.

findings.summary: The viewport configuration restricts pinch zoom and the page fails narrow reflow.
findings.evidence: Viewport meta includes maximum-scale=1; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport, and the 360 px layout had 360 px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale, permit user zoom, and fix the 360 px reflow failure.

findings.summary: Catalog images omit intrinsic dimensions and are frequently oversized.
findings.evidence: Images primitive found all 32 inspected images lacked width/height, 24 were over 2× display width, and Lighthouse failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio and tighten srcset/sizes to the rendered card slots.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP policy leave avoidable security exposure.
findings.evidence: Cookies audit found five non-Secure cookies and widespread SameSite=None; CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval and an exceptionally broad host list, despite HTTPS/HSTS/nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, narrow SameSite to actual needs, remove unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline, and reduce CSP allowlists.

findings.summary: The default page load has a large advertising and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 23 third-party origins and known Google/DoubleClick trackers; the consent text names 479 partners, while HAR recorded extensive analytics and cookie-sync traffic.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential vendors until consent, reduce partner count, batch analytics, and document the minimum data purpose for each remaining third party.

findings.summary: The visible login journey offers no discoverable passkey option.
findings.evidence: The representative catalog and game detail expose Log in controls, but DOM/script inspection found no WebAuthn/passkey affordance or navigator.credentials registration path.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in/registration alongside fallback methods and request sensitive permissions only from explicit user actions.

findings.summary: Defensive policies are present but too permissive for the application surface.
findings.evidence: HSTS, nosniff and frame protection are present, but Referrer-Policy is no-referrer-when-downgrade, Permissions-Policy only declares client hints, and CSP allows unsafe script execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter, explicitly deny unused permissions, and harden CSP/Trusted Types for injection-sensitive code.

findings.summary: The installable manifest is not backed by demonstrated offline behavior.
findings.evidence: A complete standalone web manifest is linked, but the audited runtime showed no service-worker/offline fallback evidence; the core game itself depends on a remote iframe.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker for the catalog shell and provide an explicit offline/retry state for games that require the network.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes resolution and omits intrinsic sizing.
findings.evidence: 24 of 32 inspected images were more than twice their display width; seven legacy-format pixel/asset requests were observed and no inspected URL advertised AVIF/WebP explicitly.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants with accurate srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions matched to card slots.

findings.summary: Third-party advertising and analytics consume a disproportionate initial-load budget.
findings.evidence: The home load transferred 5.04 MB across 153 requests and contacted 23 third-party origins before the user reached a game.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer vendors until interaction/consent, and remove vendors that do not provide measurable user value.

findings.summary: The catalog starts with a large heap/object footprint.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 935,254 nodes and 48.38 MB self size before entering a game; post-interaction remained 946,707 nodes and 48.85 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the catalog bundles and third-party SDKs, virtualize offscreen card state, and defer providers until needed.
